external_validation: The paper reports an independent 30% validation cohort (n=39) created by a 7:3 random split of the same recruited sample; this is not validation in a separately recruited external population.
ground_truth_method: Structured face-to-face retrospective interview of whether the participant experienced at least one fall while residing in the nursing home during the preceding 12 months; binary >=1 fall versus none.
notes: Volume/article: 26, 554. The studied population was a relatively high-functioning ambulatory institutional subgroup able to walk independently without assistive devices. The authors caution against generalizing the results to residents with advanced frailty, assistive-device dependence, or severe functional impairment.
population: Ambulatory nursing-home residents aged >=80 years from four long-term-care institutions in Shanghai, China
title: Validation of World Guideline gait speed and TUG cut-offs for fall risk stratification in ambulatory nursing home residents aged ≥ 80 years: a multicenter cross-sectional diagnostic study

ground_truth_method: Heterogeneous across the reviewed studies; the review does not define one common ground-truth method.
notes: Volume/article: 4:921506. The paper reviews wearable technologies for both fall-risk assessment and fall detection. These are related but distinct tasks and must not be treated as equivalent. The review focuses especially on inertial and insole-based systems. Review methodology: PubMed and Web of Science searches; final searches completed in March 2022; Boolean search terms related to falls, wearable devices and sensor/body location. 305 records obtained; title/abstract screening using Covidence reduced this to 150 articles; after full-text examination, 21 selected studies were presented in the review. The review emphasized insole-based and inertial-sensor-based wearable systems; studies published before 2000 were excluded. The 21 selected studies are review inclusions, not a clinical participant sample size.
population: Heterogeneous populations across the reviewed fall-risk and fall-detection studies; no single study population applies to the whole review.
study_design: Narrative review using a systematic literature search process
title: Wearable Sensor Systems for Fall Risk Assessment: A Review
